newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares ease in light trade, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares ease in light trade, profit-taking.

text.p: Leading Russian shares sank in quiet trade on Wednesday on Western profit-taking, traders said, seeing little movement in the market's most liquid shares to the end of the week.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index dipped to 508.12, down from Tuesday's record 517.54, on a limp $46.2 million total market turnover.

"Many foreign investor decided to take profits," said Rossiisky Kredit Bank trader Andrei Girichev, saying he expected a quiet day on Thursday. "Russians are continuing to buy but they don't have the strength (to support the market)."

Metals producer Norilsk Nickel closed at $14.90, a hair lower than Tuesday's closing $15.00 despite reaching a peak of 15.95 earlier in the day, while national power company UES ticked down to $0.4150 from $0.4236.
Norilsk has been volatile since the company announced on Tuesday it was doubling share capital through a rights issue.
International long-distance carrier Rostelekom slipped to $4.89 from $4.95.

Some traders said the market was taking a breather after the gains made earlier in the week on the tail of Friday's sale of a quarter stake in telecoms holding company Svyazinvest, which owns a controlling stake in Rostelekom and 88 other telecoms.
But others saw a stable market with interest moving to the less liquid shares on the second and third tier on Thursday.

"The interest in general is much stronger (on the second and third tier)," said Alfa Capital director of sales Alexander Bubnovsky. "I would expect (leading shares) to go up and down but no major movements."
